## 261018.001 (r82) -- issue #170: `-sm tensor` no longer aborts when the model has to leave layers on the host (block 00 + block 09)

**Release `v12-097cf33d9-r82`**: base `097cf33d9`, canonical tip `7d238ae80`, net tree
`dc48b4a983cba245f71e60ce8825abedac8e2a45`, **12 blocks** (block 00 + 01-11).  **Block 00 amended**
(the two upstream-code hunks) and **block 09 amended** (the fork-local hook gate); no new block.
`release.json` regenerated; `validate-set.sh` green (fresh tarball, strict 12/12, tree matches).

**Issue #170** (`void-li`, 2x 7900 XTX gfx1100, **ROCm 10.1.0**, dense Qwen3.8 27B Q8_0, ctx 196608,
`-sm tensor`): abort at the warmup decode, `GGML_ASSERT(ggml_backend_buffer_is_meta(meta_buf))` in
`ggml_backend_meta_buffer_n_bufs`.  r11 worked, r12+ asserted, and `--no-op-offload`,
`GGML_OP_OFFLOAD_MIN_BATCH=1000000`, `--fit off` and ctx 147456 all avoided it.  We could not reproduce
on 3x R9700 until the free-memory figure was matched (see below).

**Root cause, and it is not an allocation failure.**  `--fit` sees the 27B Q8_0 at 196608 ctx does not
fit on 2x24 GiB and reduces `n_gpu_layers` (his r12 log: 66 -> 32/49/57/53/55/54, "offloading 54
layers").  That mixed assignment gives the CPU-offloaded layers host-resident weights, so the block-09
meta `offload_op` hook (upstream's meta device has none, which is why r11 and unpatched llama.cpp work)
moves those layers' ops onto the Meta backend -- his log says so: `resolve_fused_ops: layer 3 is
assigned to device CPU but derived kq mask flash attention is assigned to device Meta()`.  The
split-state walk then recurses into `build_attn_mha`'s `ggml_view_4d(Qcur, ...)` -> `ggml_permute(...)`
pair; the permuted view is a plain alias (`GGML_OP_NONE`, no node) whose `src[0]` (the intermediate
view) is never initialised by the gallocr (a view is initialised from `view_src`, not from `src[0]`), so
`buffer_n_bufs(NULL)` asserted.  Two more defects were behind it: a failed constituent allocation
**aborted** (`GGML_ASSERT(meta_buf_ctx->bufs[i])`) instead of returning NULL, and once that was fixed,
the hook still claimed *dense* host-weight ops, whose layer *state* (KV cache, GDN conv/ssm state) is
also host-resident -- a case the meta split-state model cannot represent (`handle_gated_delta_net`
`src_ss[5]` assert at the first wide prefill; a 5-token completion never reaches it).

**What landed.**  *Block 00 (upstream code)*: `[TAG_META_UNALLOC_ALIAS]`, an alias with no buffer is
resolved through its view chain to the buffer it will inherit and then classified normally (allocated
tensors take the byte-identical old path); and `[TAG_META_ALLOC_FAIL]` in `alloc_buffer_n`, which frees
what was built, clears the tensors' `buffer`/`data` and returns NULL.  *Block 09 (our code)*: the same
NULL handling in `alloc_buffer_usage`, the per-tensor policy branch reading the resolved buffer, and
`[TAG_META_OFFLOAD_MOE_ONLY]`: the hook claims only `GGML_OP_MUL_MAT_ID`.  No new env var.  The two
upstream-code hunks are also staged for upstream as
`upstream/UPSTREAM-PR-meta-split-unalloc-alias-and-alloc-fail.{md,patch}` (applies clean to
`097cf33d9` and builds there).

**Reproduction on a 32 GiB card** (`archive/work/issue-170-meta-alloc/`): hold 8192 MiB per device with
a small HIP allocator so the card reports 24210 of 32624 MiB free (a 7900 XTX), and the reporter's
command reproduces the assert.  Before the fix, the minimal command, his full command line and
`-ctk/-ctv f32` all aborted at the warmup decode, and a genuine KV OOM (`--fit off -ngl 99 -ctk f32
-ctv f32`), compute OOM (`GGML_COMPUTE_BUFFER_MARGIN_PCT=3000`) or weight OOM (20000 MiB fill) aborted
at the alloc asserts.

**Verification (gfx1201, 2x/3x R9700, ROCm 10.1.0, `~/bin/build-llama-rocm`, r82 tree
`dc48b4a9`).**

* Issue #170 end to end at 24 GiB parity: the minimal command and the reporter's **full** command line
  (adaptive MTP + `ngram-mod`, `--kv-unified`, `--parallel 2`, `--no-host`, `--load-mode none`) load,
  listen, and answer a **5246-token** prompt in 64 generated tokens with `HTTP 200` and coherent text
  (`prompts/prose-rdna-boosts.txt`), no assert; `-ctk/-ctv f32` likewise.  `-sm layer` and 1 GPU
  unaffected.
* Genuine OOM paths now fail cleanly, exit 1, no core, **no VRAM leak**: KV
  (`failed to allocate ROCm0 buffer of size 12884901888 (0 of 2 sub-buffers allocated)` ->
  `failed to initialize the context: failed to allocate buffer for kv cache`), compute
  (`failed to allocate compute pp buffers`), weights (`unable to allocate Meta() buffer`), and a
  **partial** failure (`1 of 2 sub-buffers allocated`).
* Coherence: same-seed greedy text **byte-identical** to the pre-change build, `1033 chars
  sha=383655591392` (dense 27B UD-Q4_K_XL, 3-GPU tensor, `prompts/reasoning.txt`, `-n 128 --seed 42
  --temp 0`).  The prefill-logit gate and the width probe are not applicable: no kernel, band or
  approximate path is touched, and the placement change only affects graphs where a dense host-weight op
  would have been claimed on the Meta device (none exist for a fully resident model on 3 GPUs).
* **`-ncmoe` regression check (the maintainer's concern)**:
  `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-IQ4_NL` (100 GB, 176.9B A3B), 2 GPUs, `-sm tensor -ngl 99 -ncmoe 48`, ctx 32768,
  4096-token prefill, `--load-mode none --lazy-mode off`: pre-gate **246.99 / 248.14** pp and
  **39.92 / 40.88** tg t/s, gated **244.46 / 246.40** pp and **39.83 / 40.68** tg t/s (inside the
  0.8 % / 2.1 % run-to-run spread), and the hook is still active (gated `--no-op-offload`: 66.25 /
  18.32).  Structural reason: under `-ncmoe` the only host-resident weights are the expert tensors,
  whose op is `MUL_MAT_ID`.
* Dense op-offload trade-off (why the gate exists rather than "never offload"): under `-sm layer`
  (upstream's mechanism, op and state on one backend) a dense CPU layer is a **7.2x prefill win**
  (797.17 vs 110.99 t/s, decode unchanged 6.43/6.45) on the same 24 GiB-parity config, so a future
  "host input of a split op" design has real upside; under `-sm tensor` it cannot run today.  Full
  residency is 1779.69 / 32.32 t/s versus ~114 / 7.3 for the 54/66 split, which is the number a 24 GiB
  user needs (quant or context, not offload policy).

**gfx1100 cross-check** (`fingon`, single RX 7900 XTX, ROCm 7.14, `build-rocm`): r82 builds there and
is **byte-identical to r81** for same-seed greedy text (`-ctk/-ctv q8_0`, `-n 128 --seed 42 --temp 0`,
`prompts/reasoning.txt`) on Qwen3.8-27B Q4_K_M (`1064 chars sha=c606b3d55f24`) and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B
Q4_K_M (`1046 chars sha=2c04f104b88e`), i.e. inert on a single device.  That box has one card, so it
cannot exercise `-sm tensor`; the reporter's retest is still the gfx1100 tensor-split confirmation.
Host-tooling note: `fingon`'s `~/bin/build-llama-rocm` does not honour `BUILD_DIR` and configures
`build/` against the **system** ROCm 7.1 clang, whose HIP backend crashes on `unary.cu`
(`Cannot select: bf16 = uint_to_fp`).  That is the Fedora-7.1-header trap from `AGENTS.md`, not a code
problem: building in the existing `build-rocm` (configured with `/opt/rocm-7.14-gfx1100/lib/llvm/bin/clang`)
is clean.

**Issue reply**: posted 2026-10-18 (`#issuecomment-6248869022`), draft kept in
`archive/work/issue-170-meta-alloc/COMMENT-2026-10-18.md`.

**Published.**  Tag `v12-097cf33d9-r82` pushed (annotated, on the release commit); CI
**Validate delivery set** green on both `main` and the tag, **Release patch set** green (assets
`rdna-boosts-all.patch`, `patches.tar.gz`, `release.json`, `SHA256SUMS`).  The personal fork's
`rdna-boosts` branch was re-cut from `097cf33d9` with the block chain and force-pushed
(`--force-with-lease`, personal fork only); a fresh `git fetch origin rdna-boosts` reports tree
`dc48b4a9`, matching `release.json`.  The ROCm container images are built and pushed off-host by the
worker watcher (`scripts/container-watch.sh` on `radiance`), which polls for the new tag.  The staging
branch `fix-170` in `~/llama.cpp` is superseded by the canonical `rel82` chain (the delivery now
carries the same code in blocks 00/09).

## 261017.008 (r81) -- rope + FWHT fusion on M-RoPE, the q8_0 K/V cache write folded into it, paired GDN q/k norms (PRs #175, #173, #179); #177 rejected

**Release `v12-097cf33d9-r81`**: base `097cf33d9`, canonical tip `d86db8c92`, net tree
`0c3a4413131c2b1e8fab208c5d6bf7aa8cf7ba4a`, **12 blocks** (block 00 + 01-11).  **Block 10** amended, no new
block (`patches/0010-*`, message extended with the four folded patches).  `release.json` regenerated;
`validate-set.sh` green (fresh tarball, strict 12/12, tree matches).

**What landed (all bit-identical, from five contributor PRs reviewed together):**

* **#175 0001** -- `GGML_ROPE_TYPE_MROPE` / `IMROPE` admitted to `ggml_cuda_should_fuse_rms_norm_mul_rope`,
  with theta computed in the kernel from `rope_multi`'s own section selection (NEOX pairing, `n_offs == 0`,
  VISION still rejected).  This is the TODO item recorded against #172 (the MROPE gap): it is what makes
  the rope-fusion class reach the Qwen3.x models instead of only Gemma4 / gpt-oss-20b.
* **#175 0002** -- a **BF16** `SET_ROWS` is declined by the 5-op `RMS_NORM, MUL, ROPE, VIEW, SET_ROWS`
  match.  That fusion runs `ggml_cuda_op_rms_norm_mul_rope_fused`, which writes F32 / F16 rows only and
  otherwise aborts, while `ggml_cuda_should_fuse_rope_set_rows` admits BF16: a latent abort on r80 for a
  NEOX qk-norm model with `-ctk bf16`, and reachable for the Qwen3.x models once 0001 lands.  **Checked:
  0001 alone aborts at `rope.cu:1087` on the 27B with bf16 KV; 0001 + 0002 is clean and byte-identical to
  r80.**  (No model on this box reproduced the pre-0001 abort: Gemma4 12B and gpt-oss-20b with bf16 KV are
  clean on stock r80, so the latent half is unverified here -- the 0001-reachable half is not.)
* **#173** -- the q8_0 K and V cache writes folded into the fused rope kernel (warp 0 quantizes the rotated
  K row from its FWHT registers, each block its slice of the V row, through
  `ggml_cuda_quantize_q8_0_group`, i.e. `k_set_rows_q8_0_group`'s body moved into `set-rows.cuh`).  Only the
  K write is folded inside a concurrent-stream region (`GGML_CUDA_GRAPH_OPT=1`).  This is the PR rejected at
  r78 because its matcher could not fire; #175 is what makes it reachable (qwen35/qwen35moe use the
  non-iSWA `build_attn`, which expands K last), exactly the re-entry condition recorded then.
* **#179** -- the GDN q and k l2 norms in one `rms_norm_scale_pair_f32<256>` launch (blocks `[0, nrows)` q,
  `[nrows, 2*nrows)` k, same per-row body).  Matcher: no-op nodes only between the two pairs, both inputs
  F32 views of one `view_src` with equal shape/strides/eps/scale, and the second input must not read the
  first pair's output.
* Kill switches: `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_ROPE_MROPE_FUSE`, `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_ROPE_FWHT_SET_ROWS`
  (presence-only), `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_NORM_PAIR=1`.  `ENVIRONMENT.md` §7.1-§7.3 updated.

**Rejected: #177 (`gdn-conv-snapshot-fold`).**  The direct GDN conv also writing the recurrent snapshot
 tails is **not run-to-run deterministic** on this box, so it is out on purity grounds, not on speed:

* 35B-A3B Q4_K_M, 1 GPU, `test-logits-width-probe` P=256: stock r80 is stable at `W8=dfcb48a5be95c5ac`
  (5+ runs, and identical on the #175 / #179 / #173 arms); r80 + #177 gave **two distinct results in four
  runs** (`W8=48272966cab954fb`, row-0 `907b3e9c40b8c546`, and `W8=cb29e653528bddcf`, row-0
  `361d76c6d5ff877e`).  `width_purity` still reports maxdiff 0 within a run -- the difference is between
  runs, in the prefill.
* `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GDN_CONV_SNAP=1` reproduces stock exactly (`dfcb48a5be95c5ac`, twice), so the patch is
  the cause.  With `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1` the patched value is stable (`48272966...`) but still not
  stock's, so the capture path adds a second, independent divergence on top.
* Dense 27B is identical to stock at both P values, and the 400-token greedy text is stable and identical
  to r80 on 35B-A3B (3 runs), so this is a logits-level/prefill effect that the text and KLD gates do not
  see (prefill-logit KLD on both models is 0.000000 / 100.000 % for the patched arm as well).
* The **speed win is real**: 27B MTP decode 1 GPU 52.8 -> 53.3-53.4 t/s (+1.0 %); MoE 2-GPU tensor tg256
  and pp31500 flat.  Re-entry is a deterministic result; record in `archive/work/gdn-conv-snapshot-fold/`.

**Verification (gfx1201, 3x R9700, ROCm 10.1.0, `~/bin/build-llama-rocm`, r81 built from the applied set at
`097cf33d9`):**

* Same-seed greedy text **byte-identical to r80** in six arms -- 35B-A3B Q4_K_M `sha ecb4e0796ba5` (1588
  chars) and dense 27B UD-Q4_K_XL `sha 980719527364` (1719 chars), 3-GPU tensor, q8_0 KV, `--spec-type
  none` == `draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 3`, each also with `GGML_CUDA_GRAPH_OPT=1`.
* `test-logits-width-probe` PASS, worst maxdiff **0**, hashes identical to r80 at P=256 and P=3584 on both
  models (35B-A3B `dfcb48a5be95c5ac` / `411dbddc12367530`, row-0 `a44efecb25966236` / `513ac4a7cf4c5f4b`;
  27B `1dc6005a73f0e23f` / `1a12e8c36005890e`, row-0 `96905fdd2fe775ae` / `c6872278f34fa35f`).
* Prefill-logit KLD **0.000000 / 100.000 %** on both models against bases recorded from the stock r80
  build (1 GPU, ctx 512, 40 chunks, wikitext-2 test).
* `test-backend-ops`: `RMS_NORM_MUL_ROPE` **298/298**, `ROPE` 450/450, `SET_ROWS` 159/159, `RMS_NORM`
  53/53, `SCALE` 7/7, `CONCAT` 183/183, `CPY` 251/251, `SSM_CONV` 45/45.  No GPU faults
  (`scripts/check-gpu-faults.sh`).
* Launches (rocprofv3, 35B-A3B 1 GPU, 120-token decode): `rope_multi` 2500 -> 40, `fwht_cuda<256>`
  2500 -> 40, `rms_norm_f32<256,true,false,false>` 6120 -> 3660, `k_set_rows_q8_0_group` 2500 -> 20,
  `rms_norm_f32<256,false,false,true>` 7500 -> 3750; `rms_norm_mul_rope_f32<256,false,float,256>` appears

* Perf, 2-GPU tensor, 35B-A3B Q4_K_M, q8_0 KV, interleaved rounds: tg256 **114.33-114.67 -> 117.30-117.49
  t/s (+2.7 %)**; `draft-mtp` n3 `-n 400` **176.1-178.3 -> 178.3-181.3**; `pp512`, `pp31500` and
  `llama-batched-bench -npp 16 -ntg 32 -npl 1,4,8` flat (B=1 0.52-0.54 -> 0.52-0.57 s, B=4 1.23 -> 1.23,
  B=8 0.60 -> 0.60).  Dense 27B 1-GPU layer MTP decode 52.8 -> 53.2 (+0.8 %).  Per arm: #175 +1.15 %
  tg256, #179 +1.2 % (3/3 rounds), #173 +0.4 % on top of #175.
* Contributor-claim deltas: their 2-GPU tensor **+11.7 % prefill 31.5k** for #175 does **not** reproduce
  (4470 -> 4469 t/s, flat), and their 27B +0.7 % for #173 is flat here (53.1 both arms).  Everything else

**Records:** `patches/README.md` (release note + block 10), `ENVIRONMENT.md` §7.1-§7.3,
`archive/work/mrope-rope-fusion/`, `archive/work/kv-cache-q8-write/RESOLUTION.md` (updated: the r78
rejection is resolved by #175), `archive/work/gdn-l2-norm-pair/`,
`archive/work/gdn-conv-snapshot-fold/` (rejected).  PR #169 (`spec-batch-budget`) stays open and unchanged:
none of these three fusions touches the >8-row verify path that governs its verdict.

**Cross-arch check on gfx1100 (RX 7900 XTX, ROCm 7.14, native Linux, `fingon`).**  The same four patches
were re-cut and built there from the `/opt/rocm-7.14-gfx1100` tree (not the Fedora 7.1 headers) and gated
against a **stock r80 reference built from the same sources with the four patches reverse-applied**
(`git write-tree` = `873d033563e3a33eb680be65695eaf63aa90db16` = `release.json.base_tree`'s applied tree, so
the reference is exactly r80):

* Same-seed greedy text **identical to r80** (300 tokens, q8_0 KV, 1 GPU, layer) on three models:
  Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B `sha f5af07dc6502`, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q4_K_M `sha 86b1b02d18a0`, Qwen3.8-27B Q4_K_M
  `sha 3b949b9d64ea`.
* `test-logits-width-probe` PASS maxdiff **0** with **identical** W8 and row-0 hashes to r80 at P=256 and
  P=3584 on both the 30B-A3B and the 35B-A3B (e.g. 30B-A3B P=256 `W8=a5097bc9ad1f13e1`,
  `row0=98a558d45f81e80a` in both builds).
* **The stock-r80 bf16 abort reproduces here, and r81 fixes it.**  Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B (NEOX qk-norm)
  with `-ctk bf16 -ctv bf16` aborts on stock r80 at `rope.cu:1050`; on r81 the same command completes
  (128 tokens, and at 64 tokens 136.0 t/s) and the q8_0 arm is identical to r80.  This closes the
  verification gap recorded above: the abort #175 0002 guards is not only the fused-kernel one
  (`rope.cu:1087`, reachable once M-RoPE is admitted), it is also reachable on the r80 tree through the
  5-op fusion on a NEOX qk-norm model.
* Speed (1 GPU, layer, q8_0 KV, 2 rounds each, `llama-bench`): 35B-A3B tg256 **126.70 / 126.60 ->
  128.80 / 128.88 t/s (+1.7 %)**, pp512 flat (4113 / 4411 -> 4406 / 4350); dense 27B tg256
  **41.69 / 41.68 -> 42.11 / 42.09 (+1.0 %)**, pp512 1313 / 1304 -> 1305 / 1295 (flat within noise).
  So gfx1100 gains roughly what gfx1201 does and nothing regresses.

**Addendum (same day): our host link is PCIe 5.0 x4 per card, so a tensor-split prefill claim cannot be
measured here.**  Following a note from the maintainer, the topology was checked and it matters for the
one figure above that did not reproduce.  Each R9700 sits behind its own PCIe switch with a **x16 @ 32 GT/s**
device-side link but a **x4 @ 32 GT/s uplink to the host** (`current_link_width` = 4 on `0000:01:00.0`,
`0000:04:00.0`, `0000:07:00.0`; the root ports `00:01.1` / `00:01.2` are x4 too).  The contributor's boxes
are x8 (his R9700 pair) and x16 (the 7900 XTX on PCIe 4.0), so his cross-device bandwidth is 2-4x ours.

Two measurements say our multi-GPU prefill is link-bound, not GPU-bound (r81, 35B-A3B Q4_K_M, q8_0 KV,
`llama-bench -p 31500 -n 0 -r 3`): 1 GPU **3613.8** t/s, 2 GPU tensor **4481.5 (+24 %)**, 3 GPU tensor
**4347.0 (+20 %, i.e. 3 % below 2 GPU)**.  `wip/three-gpu-performance/` sees the same +17 % / +1 % shape on
the field config, so this is the host, not a model.

That qualifies the #175 prefill verdict above but does **not** change it.  Isolating the fusion itself with
its own kill switch in the r81 binary (same build, so the link cost is identical in both arms):

| prefill, 35B-A3B q8_0 | r81 default | `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_ROPE_MROPE_FUSE=1` | delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 GPU layer, pp31500 | 3613.8 | 3579.1 | +0.97 % |
| 2 GPU tensor, pp31500 | 4481.5 | 4471.4 | +0.23 % |
| 3 GPU tensor, pp31500 | 4347.0 | 4334.3 | +0.29 % |
| 2 GPU tensor, real 31.5k prompt, `-ub 2048` | 5258.5 / 5247.4 | 5241.2 / 5237.9 | +0.2-0.3 % |

So the fusion is worth about +1 % of prefill on one card and +0.25 % on a tensor split on this box; a
+11.7 % reading cannot be attributed to it here even allowing for the link.  The honest statement, now
recorded in `AGENTS.md` (Critical facts) and in the campaign note, is that the contributor's figure is
**not measurable on our link width**, not that it is refuted, and that decode claims do carry over (the
per-token all-reduce traffic is negligible, which is exactly why the +1.15 % tg256 gain reproduced at
2-GPU tensor while this did not).

## 261017.007 -- beta 12: `slab-transient-absorption` staged for a beta test, and `apply-all.sh --include-beta`

**No release change** (`release.json` untouched, no block amended, no tag).  New: `beta/0012-slab-transient-
absorption/` (candidate patch + `README.md` + `BETA-TESTING.md`) and an **opt-in** `--include-beta` flag on
`scripts/apply-all.sh`.

**Why a beta and not a block.**  The candidate (the WIP campaign summarised in
`archive/work/slab-transient-absorption/README.md` §8-§10.14) moves *where the ROCm transients live*: the H2D ring,
the FA prefill staging arena, the QSA3 and chunked-GDN prefill scratch and the workspace pool's large prefill
temporaries now come out of the slab's wide band, the per-graph caches (MMB activation + producer slots, BF16
src1) are released at the end of a compute, the MTP draft reserve is derived from the draft's own GGUF instead
of a flat constant, `--fit` reserves it, and `GGML_CUDA_SLAB_HEADROOM_MIB` becomes `512 + 128 x n_gpu`
(640/768/896 MiB) with the draft reserve charged per device under an equal `-sm tensor` split.  It is measured
(+4.0 GiB of arena on the field config, every measured topology at or above a 300 MiB outside cushion) but the
failure mode of getting a memory lifetime wrong is a hard VRAM abort on a configuration nobody has tried, so it
waits for independent validation on other RDNA families / ROCm lines / models.  This is the same holding area
that carried `beta/mmb-general` and `beta/tensor-fit-fix`.

**`--include-beta`** applies every `beta/*/*.patch` (sorted) *after* the release blocks and *after* the
`release.json` tree assertion, one commit each with the same strict-`git am`-then-one-`-3`-retry discipline, and
then reports the resulting tree (which is deliberately not the release tree).  Without the flag the script is
byte-identical in behaviour: 12 blocks, tree checked against `release.json`.

**Verified on a fresh checkout at `release.json.base` (`097cf33d9`), canonical toolchain
(`~/bin/build-llama-rocm`, ROCm 10.1.0, clang-24, ccache):**

* `apply-all.sh .` -> 12/12 strict, tree `873d033563e3a33eb680be65695eaf63aa90db16` = `release.json` (no
  regression from the flag).
* `apply-all.sh --include-beta .` -> **13 commits**, strict (no `-3`), tree
  **`18bb050f3ff2d47c54352c8ac04a986d4a4c4349`** (recorded in the beta `README.md`); builds clean; the 35B-A3B
  same-seed greedy text is **identical** to the r80 baseline and `gate-prefill-logits.sh` reports **mean KLD
  0.000000 / 100 % same-top-p**.

Patch: `beta/0012-slab-transient-absorption/0012-rdna-boosts-beta-12-slab-transient-absorption.patch`, cut
against `release.json.tip` (`00f4b1ef8`), sha256
`5f5110659ed2274e1d48942188331da187507c8e6143d75169ef3d6eed882640`.

**Not yet tested (the beta's purpose):** gfx1100/gfx1151, ROCm 7.14, dense-only and non-Qwen model families,
an unequal `-ts` split under `-sm tensor` (it takes the conservative path today), and third-party configs.
A confirmed or refuted result moves the candidate to `archive/work/` with a `RESOLUTION.md`.

## 261017.006 -- where the ~10 GiB of arena gap against Strata actually is, and the two levers that close part of it

**No release change** (`release.json` untouched, no block amended, no tag; `ENVIRONMENT.md` and the
campaign record updated).  Follow-up to 261017.005: the r80 field run showed the same arena as r79
(15 666.6 MiB), so the question was what Strata spends its VRAM on to fit 25.46 GiB.

**The gap is five buckets, measured from both engines' logs on the same card and model** (full table in
`wip/moe-cache-coverage/FINDINGS-2026-10-17-coverage-vs-defrag.md` §6.1): ~4.1 GiB idle headroom (ours;
they leave 584 MiB free), +2.2 GiB MTP draft (we load a Q8_0 draft GGUF with its own KV and compute;
they use 2-bit draft experts + a 417 MiB Q5_K head), +2.2 GiB an always-mapped narrow compute region
(1 792 MiB + 512 MiB; their decode buffers are ~70 MiB), +1.6 GiB KV (we hold the whole 131 072-cell
window; they keep 32 768 of 131 072 cells resident and stream the rest from pinned RAM), +0.4 GiB dense
weights.  **Our prefill ring/wide band is already borrowed from the arena and returned** -- the code says
so (`ggml-cuda-slab.cu:126-132`) and the field run shows the first prefill evicting 6 150 MiB and
`moe_cache_rearm` restoring the arena, which is Strata's slot-loan mechanism.  The difference is that
their *decode-time* buffers are tiny.

**Two levers measured on the idle box, same command, same model (1 GPU):**

1. **`GGML_CUDA_SLAB_HEADROOM_MIB` is worth ~1 pt of hit rate per GiB moved into the arena.** 4096 (the
   default) -> arena 15 666.6 MiB / hit 0.9056; 3072 -> 16 705.7 / 0.9147; 2048 -> 17 744.8 / 0.9223
   (16 KB prompt, 400 generated, cold start).  On a 16 384-token prompt: 0.9165 -> **0.9380** at 2048,
   generated text identical, arena re-armed to the larger size, no warnings.  **The default stays 4096**
   (the earlier 3072 rejection was `-ub 6144 -c 204800`); `ENVIRONMENT.md` now carries this measured
   envelope as a per-config tuning value.
2. **The r80 heat map is worth +1.4 pts of hit rate** -- isolated at a fixed arena and workload
   (`MOE_EXPERT_HEATMAP=0` 0.9022 vs `=load` 0.9163, same 434 760 reaches).  Pre-r80 both arms were the
   same configuration (a poisoned map ranked by expert id), which is why the r74 -> r80 field number
   looked unchanged: the feature had been delivering nothing.

**Structural, not measured:** a smaller MTP draft (Q4/Q2 experts) returns ~1.5-2 GiB to the arena; KV
window streaming (Strata's `--kv-resident 32768`) returns ~1.3 GiB more and is an engine campaign of its
own (llama.cpp has no equivalent; `--cache-ram` is idle-slot offload, not residency).

**Housekeeping for the next session.**  `archive/work/slab-transient-absorption/` (r60-era) was re-verified
against r80: new §1a table (current line numbers, measured sizes, and three rows it was missing -- the
cuBLAS workspace, the `ggml_cuda_pool_leg` high-water, and the 512 MiB H2D calibration peak), and §1b
corrects F1 -- `ggml_cuda_slab_extend` is **not** dead when an MTP draft is present (`reserve = headroom +
aux`, so the field log shows `va_spare = 4.00 GiB`); it is dead only with `aux == 0`.

**Records.** `wip/moe-cache-coverage/FINDINGS-2026-10-17-coverage-vs-defrag.md` §6.1, `ENVIRONMENT.md`
(`GGML_CUDA_SLAB_HEADROOM_MIB`), `archive/work/slab-transient-absorption/README.md` §1a/§1b.

## 261017.005 (r80) -- the MoE heat map doubled itself into saturation; the campaign retargets to "coverage" and the heat map is re-recorded (block 09)

**Delivery change.**  `release.json` is now `v12-097cf33d9-r80` (base `097cf33d9`; canonical tip
`00f4b1ef8a1895c539a589ff18d8428a6dc20abb`, net tree `873d033563e3a33eb680be65695eaf63aa90db16`; 12 blocks;
`validate-set.sh` green -- checksums OK, strict 12/12 `git am`, applied tree equals the recorded tree).
**Block 09 amended, no new block.**  **Default on.**

**The bug.**  `heat_apply_loaded_locked()` loads the persisted prior *into* `t.heat` at table
registration, the session then adds to the same vector, and every debounced save did
`g_heat_loaded[key] += t.heat` -- the whole running total.  So `loaded_k = 2*loaded_{k-1} + new`: the map
**doubled per flush** and saturated at `0xffffffff` in ~6 flushes (~6 min at the 60 s debounce).  Because
`apply_heat_seed_locked` and `alloc_all_locked` both read that prior back, **both r60 features silently
degenerated to expert-id order** (ties break `a < b`) while still logging `heat-seeded 196/196 slots`.
Measured (gpt-oss-20B MXFP4, `-ncmoe 99`, 4 GiB arena, 3 server turns, `MOE_EXPERT_HEATMAP_DEBOUNCE_S=0`,
each turn 8 016 tallies, session total 41 172): delivered **25 140 -> 58 296 -> 99 468**, fixed
**25 140 -> 33 156 -> 41 172 = the session total**.  On disk, 3 of 7 sidecars were already poisoned
(97.6 %, 99.05 %, 24.06 % saturated; a saturated map's coverage curve collapses to `H(f) = f`), including
the maintainer's Flash-Next GSQ map -- every pre-r80 measurement of a heat-seeded or heat-ordered layout
measured noise.

**The fix.**  `table_t::heat_merged` records the part of `t.heat` already folded into `g_heat_loaded`
(seeded to the prior at registration); `heat_merge_into_loaded_locked()` adds the **delta**.  **Guard at
load:** a degenerate prior (any `0xffffffff` entry -- 4.29e9 hits on one expert is unreachable -- or an
all-tied map) is ignored with one `WARN` and the run starts neutral; a **writable** file is re-recorded
from the session, a **read-only** file is left byte-identically untouched (both arms verified).  `MHT1`
stays version 1.  No kernel, arithmetic or allocation change.

**Validation.**  Heat growth linear + equal to the session total; both degenerate arms log the intended
`WARN` and emit no `heat-seeded`; the read-only file's sha256 is unchanged after the run; same-seed
gpt-oss-20B text **identical** (`sha d8588b2c8009`, 175 chars) across cold / seeded / `MOE_EXPERT_HEATMAP=0`;
prefill-logit **0.000000 / 100.000 %**; field GSQ command unchanged (arena 15 666.6 MiB, 38.3 %
residency, hit **0.9056** / 724 928 of 800 520, vs r74/r79's 0.9057).

**Toolchain gotcha for the KLD gate.**  The recorded base is **toolchain-specific**: a ROCm **10.1** build
run against the base recorded on **7.14.1** reports KLD **0.057 / 93.4 %** -- the toolchain delta, not a
regression (the 7.14.1 build of the same tree is 0.000000 / 100.000 %).  Compare like with like, or
record a base per toolchain.

**Campaign retarget (same session).**  `wip/moe-arena-defrag/` -> **`wip/moe-cache-coverage/`** (README,
`TODO.md` #61 and `wip/CAMPAIGNS.md` rewritten): the defrag premise is refuted (arena ~100 % allocated in
slots, 0.51 % truncation, 3.0 % eviction churn over a field turn, so a repack wins <= 0.5 % of bytes and
invalidates captured graphs).  The hit-rate gap against Strata is **accounting + arena size**: equal-basis
91.9 % vs our 90.6 %, and their 63.7 % residency is 25.46 GiB of arena against our 15.30 GiB.  The clean
Flash-Next map re-recorded on this build (5 669-token prompt, 0 saturated, `H(0.5) = 0.952`) gives
`H(38.3 %) = 88.7 %` -- **our 90.56 % is +1.8 pts above the static top-f bound**, and Strata's 98.4 % at
63.7 % is 98.7 % on the same curve.  Also corrected: per-layer capacity allocation is worth **0.3-0.5
pts**, not 1.5-1.9 (the 35B-A3B spread was a decode-identity tally-gap artifact).  Next phases: an offline
routing-trace replayer, then metric parity; the arena-size lever is `archive/work/slab-transient-absorption/`.

**Records.**  `wip/moe-cache-coverage/FINDINGS-2026-10-17-coverage-vs-defrag.md` (the full review,
including the Strata metric forensics), `tools/heatmap-audit.py`, `tools/heat-growth-test.sh`,
`tools/record-gsq-heatmap.sh`.

## 261017.004 -- PR #169 (`spec-batch-budget`) re-assessed on r79: still rejected, but the r77 rejection's test scope was too narrow and it exposed a verify-width cliff

**No release change** (`release.json` untouched, no block amended; nothing shipped).  PR #169 was
re-opened because five releases landed after the rejection; the question was whether its verdict depended
on commits that were missing at r77.  **It did not:** r77's two kernels were already in the rejection
build, r78's rope/FWHT fusion is inert on `rope_multi` Qwen, r78's ADD fold is `ne[1] == 1` only, r79's
MoE Q4_K VDR-4 is RDNA3_0-only on gfx1201 (RDNA4 is a build-time opt-in, off) and the r79 KV pad is
prefill-only.  Re-measured on r79 with one binary (r79 + #169), the r77 numbers reproduce: MoE 35B-A3B
3-GPU **-4/-15 %**, 2-GPU neutral, dense 27B 3-GPU **-18/-22 %** at 4 concurrent.

**What the r77 review got wrong was coverage, not commits:** every arm was all-in-VRAM.  On the
contributor's shape (host-resident experts) the cap is a large win: Flash-Next GSQ-IQ3_XXS, 2 GPUs,
`-sm tensor --n-cpu-moe 47`, shared Q8_0 MTP head, 4 concurrent 300-token requests: unset **76.5 / 87.0 /
84.5 t/s** vs `LLAMA_SPEC_BATCH_BUDGET=8` **145.7 / 145.6 / 155.2 t/s** (+80-90 %); `=12` neutral; 2 slots
still -8.4 %.  Plain decode on that config is 167.5 t/s, so the shipped default runs multi-slot MTP
*slower than no speculation* there.

**Mechanism: a verify-width cliff at `MMVQ_MAX_BATCH_SIZE == 8`.**  Per-step cost on that shape: width 4
6.0, width 8 6.4-6.9, width 12 11.5-12.2, width 16 11.5-13.0 ms per accepted token.  Flat across 8 -> 16
all-in-VRAM on 3 GPUs (5.29 vs 5.17) and on 35B-A3B with host experts (2.85 vs 2.71), so it is specific to
**qwen4exp + host-resident experts + 2-GPU tensor**; disabling the fused shared-expert epilogue does not
remove it.  **This is a delivery defect in its own right, in the default config with no env var**; the
PR's cap is a workaround for it.  Correctness: 300 tokens/request by construction (no truncation), text
coherent, cap 1 vs cap 3 **byte-identical at 2 slots**, 4-slot arm-to-arm drift is the known
concurrent-batching nondeterminism, GPU-fault check clean.

**Contributor reply** (PR #169 comment 6234999977): retracts the +8.7 % as unpaired, reports a paired
8-round +3.47 % [+2.03, +4.92] on Flash-Next GSQ **IQ3_S** with the same `-ncmoe 47` 2-GPU shape, agrees
it is not shippable as-is and offers the controller work.  Same shape, different magnitude from ours.

**Record / retest kit.** `archive/work/spec-batch-budget/RESOLUTION.md` (the re-assessment section, the
width sweep, the commits table above) plus `retest/` -- `README.md` (build, per-arm commands, pass
criteria, pitfalls, and where a revised patch gets re-measured), `run-arms.sh` (every arm as one
command, in sets) and `results/` (all 33 runs: per-run jsonl, per-slot text with sha256, and
`SUMMARY.md`).  The probe itself stays at `multislot-mtp-probe.py` because the PR comment links it.  Not promoted to a `wip/`
campaign on the maintainer's call: the PR author is taking the refinement, and the >8-row verify cliff is
recorded here as the finding to pick up.  No `TODO.md` item opened.

## 261017.003 -- docs: the canonical local build is `~/bin/build-llama-rocm` (ROCm 10.1.0); `EXTRA_CMAKE_FLAGS="-DCMAKE_HIP_FLAGS="` is now actively wrong

**No release change** (`release.json` untouched, no block amended).  Documentation-only fix, but it was
blocking work: the policy layer still instructed agents to build with
`BUILD_DIR=build-rocm-hybrid EXTRA_CMAKE_FLAGS="-DCMAKE_HIP_FLAGS=" ~/bin/build-llama-rocm-714`, which is
wrong in three ways today.

1. **Wrong toolchain.**  The canonical local source build is **`~/bin/build-llama-rocm`** (ROCm
   **10.1.0**, `/opt/rocm-10.1.0-gfx120X`, `BUILD_DIR=build-rocm`).  `build-llama-rocm-714` (ROCm 7.14.1)
   still exists and is valid for a 7.14-specific check, but it is not the default; `AGENTS.md` named it as
   *the* build in four places.
2. **The `EXTRA_CMAKE_FLAGS` override now aborts the configure.**  Both scripts pass a joined
   `-isystem<rocm>/include` in `CMAKE_HIP_FLAGS` and then verify the flag reached
   `ggml-hip/CMakeFiles/flags.make` and that `<hip/hip_bf16.h>` resolves from that tree (the
   include-order guard).  An `EXTRA_CMAKE_FLAGS="-DCMAKE_HIP_FLAGS="` clears the flag and trips the
   guard: `error: ...flags.make does not carry -isystem/opt/rocm-.../include`.  The CMake >= 4.3 problem
   the override was introduced for (a bare `-mllvm` swallowing the injected `--cuda-host-only`) no
   longer exists -- neither script passes `-mllvm`.
3. **The build dir is no longer wiped.**  The scripts reuse `BUILD_DIR` incrementally and only `rm -rf`
   it when `clean` is passed (ccache makes even a wiped rebuild cheap).

**Changed:** `AGENTS.md` (Common tasks -> "Build the fork": canonical command, the `clean`/reuse rule and
an explicit "do not override `CMAKE_HIP_FLAGS`" note; the three other `build-llama-rocm-714` mentions),
`CONTAINERS.md` and `ENVIRONMENT.md` (ccache/clang cross-reference), and the three live `wip/` campaigns
that carried the stale command line (`kv-cell-offset-nondeterminism/README.md` +
`PROMPT-kv-cell-offset.md`, `rs-rollback-boundary/README.md`).  Dated records (`WORKLOG.md`,
`archive/`, the benchmark notes) keep the command that was correct when they were written.

## 261017.002 (r79) -- Q4_K VDR-4 for the MoE expert kernel (PR #167, blocks 07/10; RDNA3_0 default-on, RDNA4 opt-in) and `LLAMA_KV_N_PAD_PREFILL` default-on for a multi-device split (block 10)

**Delivery change.**  `release.json` is now `v12-097cf33d9-r79` (base `097cf33d9`; canonical tip
`8408293e2`, net tree `c9ed11139a9a1e469bff18b037aef9cc1b0b2c93`; 12 blocks; `validate-set.sh` green --
checksums OK, strict 12/12 `git am` on a fresh tarball, applied tree equals the recorded tree; blocks 07
and 10 amended, no new block).  **PR #167 (`@briansp2020`, `rdna3-mmvq-moe-q4k-vdr4`) accepted**, and
the PR #168 follow-up is folded into the same release.

**PR #167 block 07 (`vecdotq.cuh`) + block 10 (`mmvq-vecdot.cuh`).**  The MoE expert kernel
(`mul_mat_vec_q_moe`) took `vec_dot_q4_K_q8_1_vdr4`, which scales and converts each 8-element chunk
separately.  `vec_dot_q4_K_q8_1_vdr4_dense` has the same 32-element layout and VDR 4, but sums each
sub-block's 16 products in one integer `dp4a` chain before the single scale / convert / fma.  It is now
**default on RDNA3_0** (patch 0001) and an **RDNA4 build-time opt-in**
(`-DGGML_HIP_RDNA4_Q4K_MOE_VDR4`, default off; patch 0002, separate from #162's dense flag).  The MoE
VDR is 4 either way, the selector is width-uniform, and the pinned fusion ops keep plain `calc_nwarps`;
only the intra-sub-block summation order changes.  Patch 0002 also defines a host-visible
`ggml_cuda_rdna4_q4k_moe_vdr4` constant, so ccache keys the HIP object on a device-only flag (without
it the unchanged object was returned for the flag toggle).

**PR #168 follow-up, block 10.**  `LLAMA_KV_N_PAD_PREFILL` now defaults to **8192** when more than one
device is in use (`model.n_devices() > 1` or the meta split state has more than one device) and stays
inactive on a single device.  The env value still overrides and `0` disables.  The r77 reason for
keeping it opt-in was the single-GPU **-0.35 %** prefill loss; that shape is now inactive, so the
multi-GPU win ships by default.  Decode/verify keep the decode pad and the extra cells stay masked, so
the decode numerics are unchanged.

**RDNA4 (gfx1201, 3x R9700, ROCm 7.14.1).**  Patch 0001 is RDNA3_0 only, so the default release is
**byte-identical to r78** on MoE 35B-A3B and dense 27B (only the build banner differs); the prefill-logit
gate against an r78-recorded base is **0.000000 / 100.000 %**, `MUL_MAT_ID` q4_K is 84/84, and

(`HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,2`): `llama-bench` tg256 **+0.06 %** (113.79 -> 113.86 t/s, flat), batched
B=1/B=4/B=8 **+0.9 / +0.5 / +1.5 %**, 4-axis MTP at `-n 3000` R **+3.4 %**, K **+0.8 %**, P **-1.65 %**,
C **-0.5 %**; KLD at `-ub 4` **0.003977 / 97.386 %** (PPL ratio 1.0002) and `none == draft-mtp n3`
byte-identical.  On **3-GPU tensor** the 4-axis at `-n 2000` was R -0.2 %, P -1.4 %, C +0.5 %, K +0.4 %.
It is not a clear default-on win, so 0002 stays an opt-in; the default RDNA4 path is unchanged.

**RDNA3_0 (gfx1100, RX 7900 XTX, independent rerun).**  Base r78 vs r79, single GPU, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B

## 261017.001 (r78) -- KV-rotation FWHT fused into the rope kernel and into the projection Q8_1 (PR #172, block 10), ADD + `rms_norm_q8_1` for one token (PR #174, block 10); PR #173 rejected

**Delivery change.**  `release.json` is now `v12-097cf33d9-r78` (base `097cf33d9`; canonical tip
`a0c4db04c`, net tree `b324d53566eb6f064c708047e4e0331c7ac5cc25`; 12 blocks; `validate-set.sh` green --
checksums OK, strict 12/12 `git am` on a fresh tarball, applied tree equals the recorded tree; one block
amended, no new block).  Three `@briansp2020` PRs reviewed against r77 on gfx1201 (3x R9700, ROCm
7.14.1); **two accepted, one rejected**.

**Accepted: PR #172 (`kv-rot-fwht-fusion`, both patches), folded into block 10.**  With a quantized KV
cache Q and K each ran `RMS_NORM, MUL, ROPE, RESHAPE, MUL_MAT(Hadamard)`, i.e. the fused rope launch plus
a `fwht_cuda` launch.  (1) A new `fwht_n` instantiation of the fused `rms_norm_mul_rope_f32` stages the
roped row in shared memory and runs `fwht_cuda`'s own transform, moved into `ggml_cuda_fwht_warp()` in
`fwht.cuh` and shared by both kernels (one helper in a header included before `rope.cu`'s
`#pragma clang fp contract(off)`, so both compile the transform under the same contraction mode).  The
matcher (`ggml_cuda_should_fuse_rms_norm_mul_rope_fwht`) requires one rotation block per head
(`n` = 64/128/256) and allows the allocator's usual exact `dst == x` alias (each block reads its whole
row of `x` before a barrier, then writes the same row; any other overlap rejects).  (2) `fwht_cuda<N, T,
has_q8_1>` also writes the following mmvq matmul's Q8_1 activation into the quantize cache with
`quantize_q8_1`'s reduction and rounding, so the attention-output projection skips its quantize launch;
the key is the mmvq launcher's (view root of `src1` = the Hadamard node, its shape/strides, stream), the
row must be a multiple of `MATRIX_ROW_PADDING`, and an already-cached entry stands the fusion down.
Kill switches `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_ROPE_FWHT` and `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_FWHT_Q8_1` (both presence-only).
Neither matcher participates in the mmvq band (`nwarps`/VDR) and no reduction-order anchor moves.
**Reachability:** the fusion needs NORMAL/NEOX rope with the norm+mul+rope chain, so on this box it is
**active on Gemma4** (and part 2 on gpt-oss-20b) and **inert on every Qwen3.x model here**, which all run
`rope_multi` (`GGML_ROPE_TYPE_MROPE`).  That is why the reporter's Qwen3-30B-A3B numbers do not
reproduce on the maintainer's models.

`cc1179bc`; block 02: `40408c28 4d93e972`; block 03: `1a803b9b 131d89e9`).

**Block 05 (FA tile).**  Four pieces, all RDNA2-only: (1) a per-DKQ RDNA2 tile config table
(`ggml_cuda_fattn_tile_get_config_amd_rdna2`) selected by `GGML_CUDA_CC_IS_RDNA2` on the host and

kernels inside the gfx1030 register file and 64 KB LDS/WGP; (3) a WGP-aware occupancy compute in
`launch_fattn` (HIP's occupancy query assumes `regsPerMultiprocessor = 32768` on RDNA2 -- a quarter of

(`v_mul_lo_u32` is quarter rate; the integer product is exact in fp32), and the Navi21
`MMVQ_PARAMETERS_NAVI21` table supplies the gfx1030 rows_per_block/nwarps values (ncols_dst 1 -> 4
waves, 2..4 -> 2 waves, 5..8 -> 4 rows/block).

**Cross-arch guarantee.**  The PR's README claimed all four add-on blocks were gfx1030-gated; two were
not (the partial-batch branch and `ggml_cuda_mmq_scale_sumi` under `#ifdef GGML_USE_HIP`).  Both are

typedef and the three FA kernels -- inert (`nullptr` / never read) off RDNA2.  PR block 04 (WMMA

## 261016.010 (r75) -- fix the H2D-ring/wide-compute alias and stop the MTP drafter sizing the ring (blocks 10/11)

**Delivery change.**  `release.json` is now `v12-097cf33d9-r75` (base `097cf33d9`; canonical tip
`ca33b8647f8f0723e5632f9909a64ed1241dd460`, net tree `8add179f9ddcc33e87e576a38670745f39aa96f0`; 12
blocks; `validate-set.sh` green -- checksums OK, strict 12/12 `git am`, applied tree equals the recorded
tree).  **No new block:** blocks 10 and 11 amended.  A release blocker found while exercising the r74
gate plan beyond what the handover ran (the r74 handover's own gates -- dense 4B coherence, a short MoE
coherence, the arena checks -- did not hit this path).

**The bug (block 10).**  r74 routed the wide (prefill) compute placement through the new
`ggml_cuda_slab_ring_layout` helper, which recomputed the ring from the mutable global
`g_slab_ring_region_bytes` (the *request*) instead of the region the slab actually **carved**
(`s.ring_region`).  The context re-applies its auto ring cap after the carve, so the request changed
(target ub 2048 -> 1201.2 MiB, carved 1216; later 975.3 MiB), the recomputed ring was 1024, and
`work_alloc` placed the wide view at 1792 MiB instead of 1984 -- **inside** the carved H2D staging ring
`[768, 1984)` -- aliasing the same VRAM.  On the 35B-A3B + host experts + MTP path the first wide
prefill then corrupted live tensors: a reproducible GPU VM fault
(`HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_APERTURE_VIOLATION` in `k_get_rows_float` on Q4_K_M; a `rope_multi` memory
fault on Q8_0), both GPUs.  r73 used `s.narrow_floor + s.ring_region` and did not crash.  Fix: `work_alloc`
and `seed_floor` use `ggml_cuda_slab_wide_offset()` = `s.narrow_floor + s.ring_region`; the carve-time
computation (which legitimately reads the request) is isolated in `ggml_cuda_slab_ring_candidate()`.

**The guard (block 11).**  The H2D-ring auto-size block in the `llama_context` constructor was guarded
only by `!model.moe_host_expert_bytes.empty()`.  The MTP draft context is built against the target model
(non-empty map) but its weights are fully resident and it never stages a host table, so it is not a ring
consumer -- yet it ran the block and overwrote the shared global with its own ubatch-derived value
(target ub 2048 -> 1201.2 MiB; draft ub 512 -> 975.3 MiB; `set_ring_cap` is last-writer-wins).  It now
excludes `cparams.ctx_type != LLAMA_CONTEXT_TYPE_MTP`, the same exclusion the narrow-floor pin and
ring-arm blocks already use.  With the guard the draft issues no ring resize at all (verified: every
`SET_RING_REGION` is the target's 1201.2 MiB; no 975.3 after the MTP context is created).

**Validation.**  Pre-fix r74, 35B-A3B `-ncmoe 40`, 2 GPU, `draft-mtp n3`, prose prompt: SIGABRT at the
first prefill on both Q4_K_M and Q8_0.  Post-fix (default and `MOE_EXPERT_CACHE_SIZE_AT_PRIME=0`,
graphs off, GDN sequential, adaptive) all clean, and `-n 3000` is **byte-identical to r73**: Q4_K_M
`sha 0225e8352231` / acc 0.71471 / mean len 3.14; Q8_0 `sha 69e8ecfffcef` / acc 0.67643 / mean len 3.03.
GSQ field arena unchanged: 1-GPU arena 15666.6 MiB at load, first-prefill eviction ~6.1 GiB, re-arm
restores 15666.6, hit ~90.3 %, 44.4 t/s; 2-GPU 35569.6 MiB (97.8 %); 3-GPU 40925 MiB (100 %).  Dense
gates (4B coherence, 27B prefill-logit, 27B adaptive-MTP) are unaffected -- no slab is armed for a
MoE-less model.

**Records.**  `archive/work/slab-ring-wide-alias/` (root cause, the `WORK_ALLOC` / `RING_LAYOUT`
evidence, the repro commands and the fix, in full).

## 261016.009 (r74) -- the MoE arena is sized at warmup and the seed stops at the prefill reclaim boundary (blocks 09/10/11)

**Delivery change.**  `release.json` is now `v12-097cf33d9-r74` (base `097cf33d9`; canonical tip
`9450cbb89b7d04885040370f29731aa2289ae7ce`, net tree `0fe32003b4014c2adf520eccc2e2ba1647ae3511`; 12
blocks; `validate-set.sh` green -- checksums OK, strict 12/12 `git am`, applied tree equals the recorded
tree).  **No new block:** blocks 09/10/11 amended vs r73, split by owning block (09 = iface header + the
cache priming sizing + the seed-floor skip; 10 = the shared slab layout helper + `reserve_wide` (records
the wide size) + `seed_floor` + the CUDA iface; 11 = the cpu/rpc iface initializers + the context hook).
Default on; `MOE_EXPERT_CACHE_SIZE_AT_PRIME=0` is the kill switch.

**The problem.**  The warmup is a single pass, so every host-expert table hits `moe_cache_table`'s
`!t.primed` early return and **no table is ever re-sighted in a decode-band pass** -- `alloc_all_locked`
was therefore never called at warmup and the arena was deferred to the first user decode.  The first
generated token then paid the whole arena allocation + heat/prefill seed (measured 446 ms of H2D on a
5.3 GiB arena, scaling with the arena).  Sizing on the priming pass alone over-committed: with the empty
context the slab's `extend_all` mapped the reserve the wide prefill/transients still needed (arena
15107 MiB, only 4 GiB free) and a later `hipGraphInstantiate` OOM'd.

**The fix.**  (1) The priming branch also calls `alloc_all_locked` (completeness-gated, so it still
cannot latch on a partial set); (2) at the priming sizing `slab_extend_all` is skipped, so the arena is
not sized against the over-mapped reserve; (3) the context records the wide (prefill) compute size
(`ggml_cuda_slab_reserve_wide`, from `backend_buf_exp_size`) and the cache **stops seeding at
`narrow_floor + ring + wide`** -- the band a wide prefill immediately reclaims.  The arena is therefore
sized to the FULL region (the boundary is not raised), but the ~6 GiB band is never pre-seeded: its
tables are the coldest (heat-ordered last), they are left empty, the first prefill reclaims them cheaply,
and they fill lazily during decode.  The seed boundary is the shared `ggml_cuda_slab_ring_layout`
helper's `wide_floor` output (also used by the real wide placement in `work_alloc`), so the seed
stop-point and the placement cannot disagree.  (An earlier r74 draft made the reservation a *persistent
boundary floor* instead; that shrank the arena budget to 9.75 GiB permanently and was reverted before
release -- see `archive/work/first-prefill-latency/`.)

**Results** (maintainer's exact GSQ command, 1 GPU, 13.8K prompt, adaptive MTP): arena **15666.6 MiB at
load** (the full 15.62 GiB region, matching the pre-session sizing), **97/144** tables seeded (the ~47 in
the reclaim band skipped), first prefill evicts **6150 MiB** (the band, unseeded), `moe_cache_rearm`
rebuilds 51 tables and restores the arena to **15666.6 MiB**, decode **75.0 t/s**.  Warmup sizing reaches
100 % table completeness in ~0.2 s at load.  (The 2/3-GPU arms must be re-measured for the corrected
design -- see the handoff.)

**Records.** `archive/work/first-prefill-latency/` (measurement, the `keep-survivors` prototype -- inert
in this config -- the seed-floor log and the failure logs).  The 3-GPU decode deficit this surfaced is
revived separately as `wip/three-gpu-performance/` (TODO #51).

## 261016.008 (r73) -- MoE heat map: one unified sidecar name per model (block 09)

**Delivery change.**  `release.json` is now `v12-097cf33d9-r73` (base `097cf33d9`; canonical tip
`08c6c53c7cc1428311b5bb6614224220aaeb2673`, net tree `7252e49b41fb67c74e6bcd4d81a7aeab2d479f44`; 12
blocks; `validate-set.sh` green -- checksums OK, strict 12/12 `git am`, applied tree equals the recorded
tree).  **No new block:** block 09 amended.

**The bug.**  The heat-map sidecar name was `<model_path>.moe-heatmap` -- the *exact* path the loader
happened to hand `moe_cache_set_host_source`, which is the shard that owns the first host-expert tensor.
For a sharded GGUF the first shard depends on load order, so runs wrote one map per shard
(`...-00001-of-00009.gguf.moe-heatmap`, `...-00003-...`, `...-00004-...`, `...-00008-...` in one
directory) and a single-file model got a redundant `<name>.gguf.moe-heatmap`.  A heat map is a per-model
prior, so a per-shard name is wrong by construction.

**The fix.**  A new `heat_map_base_name()` normalises the basename: strip a trailing `.gguf`, then a
trailing llama.cpp split marker `-NNNNN-of-NNNNN` (the exact `llama_split_path` format; the two strips are
independent, so a name with neither -- or only one -- passes through correctly).  `heat_map_open_locked`
now derives one `primary = <dir>/<base>.moe-heatmap` and uses `<base>` for the `MOE_EXPERT_HEATMAP_DIR`
and XDG-cache fallbacks too.  **Clean break:** the retired `<gguf>.moe-heatmap` name is never read or
written; a new `heat_map_warn_retired_locked()` scans the model directory and logs a `WARN` naming each
stale file and the new unified name (delete them; the map relearns from cold).  The four existing
scattered sidecars next to `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-IQ4_NL-PROJFIX` were deleted.

**Verification.**  Build OK.  End-to-end with a gpt-oss-20b symlink named
`Qwen3.8-...-00001-of-00009.gguf`: a cold run wrote `Qwen3.8-...PROJFIX.moe-heatmap` and the next run's
verbose log showed `loaded 69 heat entries from ...PROJFIX.moe-heatmap`; a no-suffix `gpt-oss-...gguf`
wrote `gpt-oss-...MOE.moe-heatmap`; stale shard-style and single-file legacy files each produced the
warning and were ignored.  `validate-set.sh` green (strict 12/12, tree `7252e49b4`).

## 261016.007 (r72) -- issue #164 follow-up: the ring must hold the largest staged expert slice (per-device), plus a 1-GPU crash fix

**Delivery change.**  `release.json` is now `v12-097cf33d9-r72` (base `097cf33d9`; canonical tip
`78740c1ca39e16296f9b8981a21106f7cd29e709`, net tree `431154256c190b64657a89c461c884a47fcfcca6`; 12
blocks; `validate-set.sh` green -- checksums OK, strict 12/12 `git am`, applied tree equals the recorded
tree).  **No new block:** blocks 09/10/11 amended.

**The bug.**  r71 auto-sized the H2D staging-ring hole from the prefill-throughput knee alone, so a model
whose *per-device expert-table slice* is larger than `ring_region / ring_slots` fell back to a cudaMalloc
staging buffer for those slots.  Once the arena has grown, `GGML_CUDA_OPTIONAL_ALLOC_MAX_FREE_PCT` (50 %)
refuses that fallback, so a large prefill after a decode streamed at roughly half speed (the reporter's
Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ4_NL `--n-cpu-moe 46`: **pp 755 t/s**, one refusal; GSQ control with a fitting ring:
1462 t/s).  The ring *was* re-armed -- only its per-slot capacity was too small.

**The fix (single source of truth).**  The per-device slice is not `table / devices`: the meta split is
granularity-rounded and measured **180 MiB / 270 MiB on one 450 MiB table with two devices** (40/60).  A
new `ggml_backend_meta_split_dev_bytes(tensor, split_state, n_devs, dev)` defines the size
(`sum_s ne[s*n_devs+dev]*nr[s]` along the split axis, scaled by `nbytes/ne[axis]`); the meta staging
(`ggml_backend_meta_stage_input`) now sizes its ring-slot request with it, and
`llama_model::max_host_expert_slice_bytes()` scans the host `exps` weights through the same split-state
callback the backend uses and takes the max.  The context sizes the hole as
`min(1/4 VRAM, max(throughput knee, ring_slots * (slice + 512)))`.  `h2d_stage_buffer` additionally serves
a slot at its real size (bump-allocated, stable VA) so the `unit` rounding cannot re-open the gap.  A
too-small explicit `GGML_CUDA_SLAB_RING_MIB` (a verbatim override) now emits a non-fatal **error** naming
the floor, but only when the slab is enabled (new `ggml_backend_dev_slab_enabled` hook).

**Results** (gfx1201, texts byte-identical to r71 throughout): IQ4_NL ring 1.47 -> **2.11 GiB**, refusals
1 -> **0**, pp 755 -> **1131**, tg 24.8; GSQ ring 1.47 -> 2.11 GiB, pp 1451, tg 45.2; reporter's full **73K
prefill after a decode: pp 1157**, 0 refusals.

**Found and fixed en route -- a 1-GPU segfault.**  `llama_meta_device_get_split_state_userdata` had no
initializer and `n_devices`/`model` are only set when the meta wrapper exists, so on a single device the
new scan read indeterminate bytes and dereferenced a garbage `model` in the `--fit` context probe.  The
struct now default-initializes (`= 0` / `= nullptr`, which also fixes the pre-existing uninitialized read
at `llama-context.cpp` `n_devices == 1`) and the scan requires `n_devs > 1 && n_devs <= 16 && model !=
nullptr`.

**Gates.**  `gate-prefill-logits.sh` PASS (mean KLD 0.000707, same-top-p 98.755 %); an explicit
host-expert prefill-logit comparison (GSQ `-ncmoe 48`, base recorded with the r71 ring 1502 MiB vs the new
auto 2.11 GiB) gives **mean KLD 0.000000, same-top-p 100.000 %**; warm 2500-decode `e12a175a6ad4` and cold
300-decode `687d15eaecea` are exact r71 matches; 3 concurrent sessions 0 NaN; 3-GPU ring 1.41 GiB; `-sm
layer` ring 3.52 GiB; dense 27B/4B no ring; Qwen3.6-35B-A3B ring 1.17 GiB.  All configurations exercised
without a refusal or a crash.

## 261016.006 (r71) -- issue #164: ring-region-guarded prefill drop, decode-only ring release, and auto ring sizing

**Delivery change.**  `release.json` is now `v12-097cf33d9-r71` (base `097cf33d9`; canonical tip
`0eae5b86a268f6bbba59364a0bf1722018e6a8f0`, net tree `dc2cc150df2a7b8242c4a8668237e91e26302bdf`; 12
blocks; `validate-set.sh` green -- checksums OK, strict 12/12 `git am`, applied tree equals the recorded
tree).  **No new block:** blocks 09/10/11 are amended (`ggml-backend{,-impl}.h`; `ggml-backend.cpp`,
`ggml-backend-meta.cpp`, `ggml-cuda/{common.cuh,ggml-cuda.cu,ggml-cuda-slab.cu,ggml-cuda-vmm.h}`;
`ggml-cpu.cpp`, `ggml-rpc.cpp`, `llama-context.cpp`).

**Issue #164 (reporter's toggle points at the r67 narrow -> wide compute-buffer drop).**  On the
reporter's config (gfx1201, 2x R9700, GSQ IQ3_XXS + shared MTP, `-sm tensor -ncmoe 16 -ub 2048`, q8_0
KV, `draft-mtp n3`) the r67 narrow -> wide drop (`if (ring_arm && n_tokens_prev < 64)`) fires even though
the slab carved **no** H2D ring hole (`ring_req=6 GiB` > `mapped` 5.62/5.75 GiB, so `ring_region=0`): the
drop only exists to force a wide view to re-place above a carved hole, and with no hole it just churns
the compute layout.  With HIP graphs on it costs ~13-16 % decode (measured r68 stock **101.8** vs the
reporter's drop-off toggle **118.2** t/s; r69 stock **100.0**; graphs off both ~104-105; identical
acceptance 0.85928, identical greedy text, identical cache hit/traffic).  Fix: a new
`ggml_backend_dev_slab_ring_region(dev)` accessor (`ring_region > 0`) and only drop when a hole exists
(`llama-context.cpp`).  Fixed on the reporter's config: **118.4-118.5** t/s, 0 evictions.

**Ring release on decode (the second finding).**  In a ring-armed config the first prefill -> decode
`drop_now` released the wide view but re-reserved the narrow one **above** the ring, because
`ggml_backend_cuda_device_slab_ring_set` skipped the disarm while `!moe_cache_is_sized()` and the cache
is only (re)armed after that reserve: the boundary fell 9472 -> 9216 MiB instead of to the 1536 MiB
narrow floor, and the width recorder then baselined at 9216 so it never re-dropped.  The 6 GiB hole was
held for the whole decode.  The gate existed to prevent an arena-sizes-into-the-hole then evict/cold
re-arm MTP NaN (`archive/work/slab-ring-region/` 9.4), but that consumer (whole-table staging **from**
the cache, `stage_from_cache`) has since been removed and the NaN no longer reproduces (GSQ and IQ4_NL
field configs, 0 NaN).  Retired the gate so a decode-only pass returns the ring+wide to the arena; the
deferred `alloc_all_locked` then sizes the decode arena across it.  Measured GSQ `-ncmoe 48`: arena
**8371 -> 33571 MiB**, hit **0.94 -> 0.985**, decode **92.3 -> 132.6** t/s (2000-token warmup + 2500-token
decode), greedy text byte-identical (`e12a175a6ad4`) and acceptance identical.  A prefill that follows
re-arms and evicts only what filled the hole while decode-only.

**Auto ring sizing (per GPU).**  The 6144 MiB `GGML_CUDA_SLAB_RING_MIB` default was the cap on a bound
derived from a *merged* host tensor, applied per device -- ~4x oversized on 2 GPUs.  Measured prefill
knees (per-device ring vs 31.5k-token pp, `-ncmoe 48`): n1 ub2048 ~3 GiB / ub8192 ~6 GiB; n2 ub8192
~1.5 GiB; n3 ub8192 <1 GiB; decode flat and text-identical across every ring size.  Auto-size when the
env is unset: `min(1800/n + ub/(1.7 n^2), 0.25 * VRAM)` MiB per GPU (n = host-expert device count,
smallest cap wins), applied in `llama_context` before `sched_reserve()` via
`ggml_backend_dev_slab_set_ring_cap`; `GGML_CUDA_SLAB_RING_MIB` stays a verbatim per-GPU override.
Validated at the formula's sizes: n1 ub2048 630 (plateau 630), n1 ub8192 2143 (2141), n2 ub2048 897
(896), n2 ub4096 1527 (1526), n2 ub8192 1917 (2000, run noise), n3 ub8192 2031 (2054).  Warm-cache #164
re-check: `-ncmoe 16` 120.2 -> **138.0** t/s, `-ncmoe 48` 92.3 -> **132.6** t/s, text byte-identical.
3 concurrent sessions (`-np 3`, `-ncmoe 48`): 0 NaN, arena 36.4 GiB.

**Gates.**  `validate-set.sh` green on a fresh tarball (strict 12/12, tree match).  Same-seed greedy text
byte-identical stock vs fix on both the no-ring (`-ncmoe 16`) and ring (`-ncmoe 48`) configs, warm and
cold.  Decode deterministic and text-identical across all ring sizes tested.  Issue #164 to be answered
and closed.

## 261016.002 (r70) -- RDNA2 (`gfx1030`) best-effort bring-up (issue #158): gfx1030 WMMA compile guards + container arch

**Delivery change.**  `release.json` is now `v12-097cf33d9-r70` (base `097cf33d9`; canonical tip
`2afc3a041`, net tree `592a097cd6cef3ef1d179f1d79441fa798a88439`; 12 blocks; `validate-set.sh` green on
a fresh tarball -- strict 12/12 `git am`, applied tree equals the recorded tree).  **No new block:**
blocks 06 and 10 are amended; the r69..r70 code diff is exactly the two guard files below.

**Why.**  Issue #158: the published image is built for `gfx1100;gfx1150;gfx1151;gfx1200;gfx1201`, so an
RDNA2 device has no code object and every kernel launch fails (`ROCm error: invalid kernel file`,
surfaced in `ggml_cuda_op_rms_norm_fused` only because that is the first kernel `ggml_cuda_try_fuse`
launches, not because the fused norm is broken).  The maintainer has no usable RDNA2 device, so RDNA2
ships **best-effort / unvalidated**; this release removes the blanket core dump and lets RDNA2 owners
pick up the generic, runtime-dispatched work.

**Guard fold (block 06 `mmb.cu`, block 10 `fattn-qsa3.cu`).**  A `gfx1030` compile audit (build-only,
ROCm 7.14.1 clang, `make -k` over the HIP backend) found exactly two failing TUs: `mmb.cu` and
`fattn-qsa3.cu`.  Both are the "portable WMMA dispatch" helper falling through to the first-gen gfx11
intrinsic in an unconditional `#else`:

```
error: '__builtin_amdgcn_wmma_f32_16x16x16_f16_w32' needs target feature wmma-256b-insts,wavefrontsize32
```

Fixed with `#else` -> `#elif defined(RDNA3)` plus a new `#else return c;` arm.  The RDNA2 arm is never
launched (`mmb_enabled()` and `ggml_cuda_flash_attn_qsa3_supported()` return false for `gfx1030`), and
the RDNA3/RDNA4 preprocessed source is unchanged (gfx1201 still takes the `RDNA4` arm, gfx1100 the
`RDNA3` arm), so their codegen is byte-identical.  After the fold the whole HIP backend and `llama-cli`
build clean for `gfx1030`, and `libggml-hip.so` carries only `amdgcn-amd-amdhsa--gfx1030` code objects.
Everything else already falls back at runtime: the `MMVQ_PARAMETERS_RDNA2` table, and the upstream
dp4a / tile-FA paths.

**Container (`.devops/rdna-rocm.Dockerfile`).**  `ROCM_DOCKER_ARCH` gains `gfx1030`.  Verified in the
`7.14.1-full` and `10.1.0-full` base images that rocBLAS carries `gfx1030` Tensile kernels (hipBLASLt
does not, but llama.cpp routes BLAS through rocBLAS unless `ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT` is set, which the
delivery does not).  The worker (`scripts/container-watch.sh`) builds and pushes the images off the r70
tag; nothing runs on the primary box.

**Docs.**  README "Supported architectures" gains an RDNA2 row and a best-effort caveat; CONTAINERS
gains an "RDNA2 (gfx1030)" section (fallbacks, guards, rocBLAS, and the `-fa on` risk: upstream RDNA2
tile-kernel defects per `sixvolts/llama-navi21-furnace`, so run `-fa off` on an abort); TODO #66 tracks
the open platform validation; the `beta/rdna2/` candidate and tester checklist move to
`archive/work/rdna2/` with the fold.

**Gates.**  Compile audit as above.  RDNA3/RDNA4 codegen is unchanged by construction, so r69's
recorded gates stand and no new runtime gate was run; RDNA2 hardware was not available.  External
confirmation is requested on issue #158.

**Published (2026-10-16).**  The delivery repo `main` was pushed (`8b2aa60..bbbe57d`) and the release
tagged **`v12-097cf33d9-r70`** (annotated, tag object `844cbebdb`); CI `Validate delivery set` and
`Release patch set` are green and the GitHub Release carries `patches.tar.gz`,
`rdna-boosts-all.patch`, `release.json` and `SHA256SUMS`.  The personal fork's `rdna-boosts` branch was
force-pushed to the same tree (`d210c73b7 -> 4686472c1`, `--force-with-lease`, fork only) from a clean
12-commit chain on the base (`applied tree 592a097cd...`, `validate-set.sh` green on a fresh tarball;
the same-seed 4B Q8_0 coherence run on that build is `f051d98e4e30`, byte-identical to r69).  The ROCm
container images (7.14.1 + 10.1, `full`/`light`/`server` + the immutable `-097cf33d9` variants,
`latest` on 10.1) are built and pushed off host by the `radiance` worker
(`scripts/container-watch.sh`), which polls the tag; nothing ran on the primary box.  Issue #158 has
the public write-up for `@slavap` and is closed.

## 261015.006 (r68) -- issue #151: async graph-input uploads default-on + per-graph GDN state-gather index

**Delivery change.**  `release.json` is now `v12-097cf33d9-r68` (base `097cf33d9`; canonical tip
`fc6dcad9f`, net tree `ffe832696698786865f4adf18216a019b61b160e`; 12 blocks; `validate-set.sh` green on
a fresh tarball -- strict 12/12 `git am`, applied tree equals the recorded tree).  **No new block:**
block 09 (`moe-expert-cache.cu`) and block 10 (`ggml-cuda.cu`, `ggml-cuda-try-fuse.{cu,cuh}`) are
amended.

**Issue #151 (`@DanoPTT`, gfx1201, Windows 11, Ryzen 5 PRO 4650G, graphs off).**  Dense decode was
1.3-2.4 % slower on r56 than on their r30 reference, with the GPU doing the same or less work, so the
cost is the eager host path.  The reporter's follow-ups narrowed it to the synchronous graph-input
upload (`GGML_CUDA_ASYNC_INPUT`) and the `O(gathers x nodes)` GDN state-gather walk
(`ggml_cuda_gdn_state_gather_deferrable`).  It does not reproduce as a version regression on our box
(GPU-bound: ~4.5 ms host/graph against their ~10), so the win is verified by host time and by their box.

1. **Async graph-input uploads now default-on (block 10, `ggml-cuda.cu`).**  `g_async_input_on` is
true unless `GGML_CUDA_ASYNC_INPUT=0`; the first-hit notice moves from `WARN` to `INFO` and names the
kill-switch.  The synchronous path blocked the host on every small graph-input copy; the async path
stages through the per-device 16 MiB pinned ring with the done-event ordering (r46/PR #125).  The
historical single-run impurity that kept it opt-in is closed by that ordering; re-validated here.
2. **Per-graph GDN state-gather index (block 10, `ggml-cuda-try-fuse.{cu,cuh}` + the loop in
`ggml-cuda.cu`).**  The walk scans every remaining node for each candidate gather (~48 gathers x
~1900 nodes on a 64-layer GDN decode graph).  The index answers every gather from one pass, built
**lazily on the first candidate** so a non-GDN graph pays only a pointer check per `GET_ROWS`.
`GGML_CUDA_GDN_GATHER_INDEX=0` selects the walk; `=2` runs both and `GGML_ABORT`s on a different answer.
The index is **conservative** relative to the walk (its fields are counted over the whole graph,
including nodes before the gather, while the walk sees only nodes after it), so a disagreement can
only drop a deferral -- the ordinary un-skipped `GET_ROWS` (bit-identical) -- never add one.
3. **The two per-table arena seed notices move from `WARN` to `INFO` (block 09, `moe-expert-cache.cu`).**
`apply_prefill_seed_locked`'s `prefill-...` line and `apply_heat_seed_locked`'s `heat-seeded ...` line
printed once per expert table at load.  ggml has no `TRACE` level; `GGML_LOG_INFO` is the `-lv 4`-only
level here (`common_log_get_verbosity(GGML_LOG_INFO) == LOG_LEVEL_TRACE`), so they are gone at the
default `-lv 3` and visible at `-lv 4`.

**Measurements (gfx1201, 1x R9700, 27B Q6_K, graphs off, `-t 8`).**  5 interleaved `-r 10` rounds on
the candidate: tg128 **24.600 -> 24.659 t/s (+0.24 %)**; r68 build 3 rounds: **24.593 -> 24.650**
(+0.23 %).  Prefill `pp4096` unchanged.  Host per graph (`GGML_CUDA_GCDBG=1`, 65 graphs / 250055
nodes): **4.97 -> 4.34 ms** for the index (**-0.63 ms, -13 %**); async removes the per-copy
`cudaStreamSynchronize` (outside `graph_compute`, so not in that timer; +0.21 % tg by itself).  The
reporter measured async **+1.4 %** over the index arm (+0.5 % over r30) and the index **+0.3 %**.

**Gates (r68 build, `fc6dcad9f`).**  `gate-prefill-logits.sh` **PASS** (mean KLD **0.000707** /
same-top-p **98.755 %**); 4B Q8_0 same-seed greedy **7386359e5dac** (== r67), identical across
`{graphs on/off} x {defaults / both kill-switches}`; adaptive-MTP `none == draft-mtp n3 == n7` prose
n3000 byte-identical (**1a80de87f2b6**); `GGML_CUDA_GDN_GATHER_INDEX=2` clean on 4B / 27B Q6_K / 27B
Swift UD-Q5_K_M / 35B-A3B (`-ncmoe 99` and `-sm tensor -ncmoe 20` 2-GPU) / Gemma4 E4B (non-GDN)+
MTP, graphs on and off; 2-GPU `-sm tensor` and `-sm tensor -ncmoe` same-seed coherent.  No correctness
risk local to this change; the residual ~0.4 % from the report is unattributed upstream
`a55e952b8 -> 097cf33d9` drift (not bisected).  Campaign record:
`archive/work/issue-151-host-path-regression/` (with `RESOLUTION.md`).

## 261015.005 (r67) -- block-09 host-expert ring arming + the r66 MUL_MAT_ID prefill regression

**Delivery change.**  `release.json` is now `v12-097cf33d9-r67` (base `097cf33d9`; canonical tip
`c536e9703`, net tree `3ccabe1522d480cef2001ee87712d56acef0d1eb`; 12 blocks; `validate-set.sh` green on
a fresh tarball -- strict 12/12 `git am`, applied tree equals the recorded tree).  **No new block:**
blocks 09/10/11 are amended.  Because block 10's refactor owns `ggml-cuda.cu`, `ggml-cuda-slab.cu` and
`mmid.cu`, and block 11 last touches `llama-context.*`, each fix is folded into the last block that owns
the file -- **09** `moe-expert-cache.cu`; **10** `mmid.cu`, `ggml-cuda-slab.cu`, `ggml-cuda.cu`; **11**
`llama-context.{h,cpp}`.  No block bodies outside those three change.

**r66 prefill regression -- root cause and fix (block 10, `mmid.cu`).**  The r66 block-00 MUL_MAT_ID
duplicate-ids fix replaced `mm_ids_helper`'s specialized templates with a generic kernel that processes
**one token per warp iteration with two warp reductions per token** (`warp_reduce_sum` +
`warp_prefix_inclusive_sum`) and reads `ids` twice; that is ~8x the r65 helper cost, and it runs once per
MoE MUL_MAT_ID.  Bisection (35B-A3B Q8_0, `-t 8 -fa on -ub 4096 -p 4096`, fully resident): r65
**8357** -> r66 **6430** t/s; dense 27B unaffected (1971 -> 1974, so MUL_MAT_ID-only); reverting the 5
MUL_MAT_ID files recovered it (8386); `mmid.cu` alone reproduced it (6473); `mmq`/`mmf` alone did not
(8337).  Fix: restore the `n_expert_used` {2,4,6,8,10,16,32} template fast path, **duplicate-correct**
-- `warp_size/neu_padded` tokens per iteration and the per-token count/rank from
`warp_reduce_sum<neu_padded>` / `warp_prefix_inclusive_sum<neu_padded>` inside the token's padded lane
group, so every repeated `(token, iex)` occurrence is its own compact row in `(token, iex)` order; the
generic kernel stays as the `n_expert_used == 0` fallback.  Recovered: fully-resident **8243** t/s (r65
8357), `-ncmoe 4` **6859** (r65 6522 -- the kept r66 `mmq`/`mmf` changes beat r65).  Correctness:
`test-backend-ops -o MUL_MAT_ID -p dup=1` **16/16**, full `-o MUL_MAT_ID` **947/947**.

**Block-09 host-expert fixes (from the `archive/work/block09-cache-ring-arming/` handover).**

1. **Cache completeness (block 09, `moe-expert-cache.cu`).**  The deferred arena sizing compares the
   **total** registered host-expert bytes against the preflight total instead of each device's even
   `bytes/n_dev` guess.  On the GSQ 40/60 split the per-device gate never latched, so the arena was
   never sized and every step streamed (GSQ `-ncmoe 48`: 14.8 -> 62 t/s).
2. **Pageable weight source (block 10, `ggml-cuda.cu`).**  `ggml_backend_cuda_buffer_set_tensor`
   bounces **any** pageable source, dropping the `usage != WEIGHTS` exemption, so the `-lm none` +
   `-sm tensor` Meta whole-tensor upload no longer issues a bare `cudaMemcpyAsync` from anonymous
   memory (the SDMA0 fault, issue #137 class; IQ4_NL 5/5 clean loads).  A pinned source still copies
   directly.
3. **Early narrow floor + ring arming (block 10 `ggml-cuda-slab.cu`, block 11 `llama-context.*`).**
   The narrow (verify) floor is pinned before the first prefill (not only at the prefill->decode drop),
   and a prefill ubatch (`n_tokens >= 64`) is placed **above** the ring even when its compute buffer is
   no larger than the narrow floor -- the 35B-A3B / GSQ layouts are size-independent, so a size-only
   test left the carved ring unarmed and the H2D staging fell back to a capped `cudaMalloc`.  A
   narrow->wide transition drops the reused narrow buffer so the prefill actually re-reserves; the width
   threshold is `< 64` to match the ring gate (GSQ's first prefill ubatch is 42 tokens).  Proof:
   `WORK_ALLOC ... narrow=0 ret_off=narrow_floor+ring_region` on all three models and
   `ring_slot_capacity > 0`.  GSQ `-ncmoe 48` prefill **645 -> 687** t/s (r65 651).

**DoD matrix (gfx1201, 2x R9700, `tools/dod.sh`, `-b/-ub 2048`, 31.5K prompt; 0 faults; ring armed on
all three; "field 70K" = the IQ4_NL 70K MTP n7 config).**
